overview:
Oracle WebLogic is a platform for developing, running and deploying enterprise Java applications both on-premises and in the cloud. It centralizes application services that include web server functionality, business components such as messaging, and access to backend enterprise systems such as databases. 

Oracle WebLogic monitoring with Datadog enables you to:
- Gain awareness of increasing heap size in your Java Virtual Machine (JVM)
- Track server response time
- Monitor session details of web applications
- Track thread pool and messaging services
- Track database connection pool usage

**Minimum Agent version:** 7.33.0
setup:
### Installation

The WebLogic check is included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package.
No additional installation is needed on your server.

1. This check is JMX-based and collects metrics from the Platform MBean Server exported by the JVM, so your WebLogic servers must have JMX Remote Monitoring enabled. See [Remote Monitoring and Management][9] for installation instructions.

2. Set the system property `-Djavax.management.builder.initial=weblogic.management.jmx.mbeanserver.WLSMBeanServerBuilder` to enable these metrics on the Platform MBean Server. This should be enabled in both the WebLogic Server Administration Console and in the server startup scripts. **Note**: This can and should be done more than once.


   _**Enable in the Administration Console**_

   ```
   Domain => Configuration => General => Advanced => Platform MBean Server Enabled
   ```

   _**Enable in Server Startup Scripts**_
 
   ```yaml
   -Djavax.management.builder.initial=weblogic.management.jmx.mbeanserver.WLSMBeanServerBuilder
   ```
      
   For more information, see the [WebLogic documentation][14].


3. Verify that the [`PlatformMBeanServerUsed`][10] attribute value is set to `true` in the WebLogic Server Administration Console. The default value is `true` in WebLogic Server versions 10.3.3.0 and above. This setting can be found in the WebLogic Server Administration Console or configured using the WebLogic Scripting Tool (WSLT). 

   _**Enable in the Administration Console**_

   ```
   Domain (<WEBLOGIC_SERVER>) => Configuration => General => (Advanced) => Platform MBeanServer Enabled
   ```
   
   _**Enable in WLST**_

   Start an edit session. Navigate to the JMX directory for the domain and use `cmo.setPlatformMBeanServerUsed(true)` to enable the attribute if it is set to `false`.

   For example:
   ```
   # > java weblogic.WLST
   (wlst) > connect('weblogic','weblogic')
   (wlst) > edit()
   (wlst) > startEdit()
   (wlst) > cd('JMX/<DOMAIN_NAME>')
   (wlst) > set('EditMBeanServerEnabled','true')
   (wlst) > activate()
   (wlst) > exit()
   ```

   Activate the changes and restart the WebLogic server.

### Configuration

1. Edit the `weblogic.d/conf.yaml` file, in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your
   Agent's configuration directory to start collecting your WebLogic performance data.
   See the [sample weblogic.d/conf.yaml][3] for all available configuration options.

   This check has a limit of 350 metrics per instance. The number of returned metrics is indicated when running the Datadog Agent [status command][4].
   You can specify the metrics you are interested in by editing the [configuration][3].
   
   To learn how to customize the metrics to collect, see the [JMX Checks documentation][5] for more detailed instructions.
   If you need to monitor more metrics, contact [Datadog support][6].

2. [Restart the Agent][7]

### Validation

[Run the Agent's `status` subcommand][4] and look for `weblogic` under the Checks section.

metrics.name: weblogic.connector_connection_pool_runtime.connections_active
metrics.description: The current total active connections.

metrics.name: weblogic.connector_connection_pool_runtime.connections_created_total
metrics.description: The total number of Connector connections created in this Connector Pool since the pool is instantiated.

metrics.name: weblogic.connector_connection_pool_runtime.connections_free
metrics.description: The current total free connections.

metrics.name: weblogic.jms_runtime.connections_current
metrics.description: The current number of connections to WebLogic Server.

metrics.name: weblogic.jms_runtime.connections_total
metrics.description: The total number of connections made to this WebLogic Server since the last reset.

metrics.name: weblogic.jms_runtime.jms_servers
metrics.description: The current number of JMS servers that are deployed on this WebLogic Server instance.

metrics.name: weblogic.jms_runtime.jms_servers_total
metrics.description: The total number of JMS servers that were deployed on this WebLogic Server instance since this server was started.

metrics.name: weblogic.jvm_runtime.heap_free
metrics.description: The current amount of memory (in bytes) that is available in the JVM heap.

metrics.name: weblogic.jvm_runtime.heap_free_percent
metrics.description: Percentage of the maximum memory that is free.

metrics.name: weblogic.jvm_runtime.heap_size
metrics.description: The current size (in bytes) of the JVM heap.

metrics.name: weblogic.jvm_runtime.heap_size_max
metrics.description: The maximum free memory configured for this JVM.

metrics.name: weblogic.server.max_open_sockets
metrics.description: The maximum number of open sockets allowed in server at a given point of time.

metrics.name: weblogic.server.threadpool_socket_readers_percent
metrics.description: The percentage of execute threads from the default queue that can be used as socket readers.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_channel_runtime.bytes_received
metrics.description: The total number of bytes received on this channel.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_channel_runtime.bytes_sent
metrics.description: The total number of bytes sent on this channel.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_channel_runtime.connections_active
metrics.description: The number of active connections and sockets associated with this channel.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_channel_runtime.messages_received
metrics.description: The number of messages received on this channel.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_channel_runtime.messages_sent
metrics.description: The number of messages sent on this channel.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_channel_runtime.sockets_accepted
metrics.description: The number of sockets that have been accepted on this channel. This includes sockets both past and present.

metrics.name: weblogic.server_runtime.open_sockets
metrics.description: The current number of sockets registered for socket muxing on this server.

metrics.name: weblogic.servlet_runtime.exec_time_high
metrics.description: The amount of time the single longest invocation of the servlet has executed since created.

metrics.name: weblogic.servlet_runtime.exec_time_low
metrics.description: The amount of time the single shortest invocation of the servlet has executed since created.

metrics.name: weblogic.servlet_runtime.exec_time_total
metrics.description: The total amount of time all invocations of the servlet have executed since created.

metrics.name: weblogic.servlet_runtime.pool_max_capacity
metrics.description: The maximum capacity of this servlet for single thread model servlets.

metrics.name: weblogic.servlet_runtime.reloads_total
metrics.description: The total count of the number of times this servlet has been reloaded.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.completed_requests
metrics.description: The number of completed requests in the priority queue.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.execute_threads_idle
metrics.description: The number of idle threads in the pool. This count does not include standby threads and stuck threads. The count indicates threads that are ready to pick up new work when it arrives.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.execute_threads_total
metrics.description: The total number of threads in the pool.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.overload_rejected_requests
metrics.description: Number of requests rejected due to configured Shared Capacity for work managers have been reached.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.queue_length
metrics.description: The number of pending requests in the priority queue. This is the total of internal system requests and user requests.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.shared_capacity_work_managers
metrics.description: Maximum amount of requests that can be accepted in the priority queue.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.threads_hogging
metrics.description: The threads that are being held by a request at the time of submission.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.threads_standby
metrics.description: The number of threads in the standby pool. Threads that are not needed to handle the present work load are designated as standby and added to the standby pool. These threads are activated when more threads are needed.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.threads_stuck
metrics.description: Number of stuck threads in the thread pool.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.throughput
metrics.description: The mean number of requests completed per second.

metrics.name: weblogic.threadpool_runtime.user_requests_pending
metrics.description: The number of pending user requests in the priority queue. The priority queue contains requests from internal subsystems and users. This is just the count of all user requests.

metrics.name: weblogic.webapp_component_runtime.sessions_current
metrics.description: The count of the current total number of open sessions in this module.

metrics.name: weblogic.work_manager_runtime.requests_completed
metrics.description: The number of requests that have been processed, including daemon requests.

metrics.name: weblogic.work_manager_runtime.requests_pending
metrics.description: The number of waiting requests in the queue, including daemon requests.

metrics.name: weblogic.work_manager_runtime.threads_stuck
metrics.description: The number of threads that are considered to be stuck on the basis of any stuck thread constraints.

serviceChecks.name: Can Connect
serviceChecks.description: Returns `OK` if the Agent is able to connect to and collect metrics from the monitored WebLogic instance, `WARNING` if no metrics are collected, and `OK` otherwise.

monitors.title: Number of active thread is high
monitors.description: Threads are a crucial mechanism to ensure that the server can efficiently manage a wide range of tasks without becoming overwhelmed. This monitor tracks the utilization of WebLogic Server's thread pool to avoid potential performance concern.

monitors.title: Number of stuck thread is high
monitors.description: A thread is stuck when it is unable to make progress and complete its task within a reasonable timeframe. This monitor tracks the number of stuck threads to identify issues affecting the performance of the application.
